answer: Unique hardware timing fingerprint. Each agent must return a nonce derived from a physical clock drift signature its operator cannot clone across machines, and a lone operator's second instance will wander off the expected drift band within hours. A fraudster must acquire and maintain one distinct physical device per identity, and any deviation leaves a plume of timing noise the verifier flags. A single fast falcon of a forged signature still fails the cross-instance drift check, so each fake identity costs real hardware plus upkeep.
